title: The London Palladium and Lawrence Brown's nerves
summary: The band opened three weeks at the Palladium; Brown was the nervous one and the opening applause shook everyone.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was that the first concert you played on that trip to Europe?
No, we played at the Palladium, I forgot; we played the Paladium first for three weeks in there.
You weren't nervous at the Palladium?
Oh, no, no. Brown was the one who was nervous.
He used to play -- I forgot the name of

that tune he used to play, and I used to go out front and play it -- he played it, but he realized he was nervous, you know? Oh, you've got to get nervous with those kind of people out there. They are expecting so much from you, and when we first started and opened the curtain and announced Duke Ellington, the applause lasted so long, you know it's gonna shake you up.
